# CETP canonical results

**This file is generated by `make results`. Do not edit it, and do not quote any number
about CETP from anywhere else.** Every figure in the paper, the deck, the LLD and the
README must come from here or from `results/canonical_metrics.json`.

- dataset: `data/corrected/tpch_dataset_corrected_v2.csv` — 5 machines × 21 queries × 20 repeats = 2100 rows → 420 ordered dev→prod pairs
- machines: c5a, c7i, m5a, r5n, z1d (**5**, all EBS-backed, SF1). Q15 excluded → 21 queries.
- environment: Python 3.13.2, scikit-learn 1.8.0, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 2.2.3; `random_state=42`, 2000 bootstrap resamples

## Headline

Leave-one-machine-out, multi-core compute signal, classifier refit inside every fold:

> **analytical roofline 21.61% MAPE vs naive-linear 23.05%** — improvement +1.44pp, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI [0.32, 2.56], excludes zero (significant).

### The qualification that must travel with the headline

`cmp_only` — scale by `1/compute_ratio` alone, with no classifier, no roofline weighting and no fitted parameters — scores **20.06% MAPE**, better than the analytical roofline's 21.61%. The paired difference is +1.55pp with CI [-0.41, 3.51], which **includes zero**.

> **The bottleneck classifier and roofline weighting are statistically indistinguishable from their own simplest component.** The gain over the bandwidth baseline is real, but it is attributable to using *compute* rather than *bandwidth* as the scaling signal — not to the classification or the weighting. Any claim that the roofline model is the contribution is unsupported by this evaluation, and `cmp_only` must be reported alongside it.

## 1. Scaling-factor accuracy

`q-error = max(pred/actual, actual/pred)`, the metric the database literature reports.
A perfect model scores MAPE 0, MdAPE 0, q-error 1.000.

## 2. Leakage audit

Every prior LOMO script loaded one globally-fit `models/bottleneck_classifier.pkl` and
applied it to held-out data. Since `p_compute/p_bandwidth/p_io/p_mixed` and
`analytical_scaling` are features, that classifier's exposure to the held-out rows leaked
into every reported number. Below: the old leaky protocol vs a classifier refit inside each
fold. Positive inflation = the old number was optimistic.

| protocol | approach | MAPE leaky | MAPE leakage-free | inflation pp |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| LOMO | naive | 31.96 | 31.96 | +0.00 |
| LOMO | naive_linear | 23.05 | 23.05 | +0.00 |
| LOMO | cmp_only | 20.06 | 20.06 | +0.00 |
| LOMO | analytical | 21.61 | 21.61 | -0.00 |
| LOMO | gated | 22.32 | 22.32 | +0.00 |
| LOMO | learned | 25.62 | 23.90 | -1.72 |
| LOQO | naive | 31.96 | 31.96 | +0.00 |
| LOQO | naive_linear | 23.05 | 23.05 | +0.00 |
| LOQO | cmp_only | 20.06 | 20.06 | +0.00 |
| LOQO | analytical | 21.61 | 21.66 | +0.05 |
| LOQO | gated | 22.32 | 22.79 | +0.48 |
| LOQO | learned | 17.04 | 17.29 | +0.25 |
| LOMQO | naive | 31.96 | 31.96 | +0.00 |
| LOMQO | naive_linear | 23.05 | 23.05 | +0.00 |
| LOMQO | cmp_only | 20.06 | 20.06 | +0.00 |
| LOMQO | analytical | 21.61 | 21.64 | +0.02 |
| LOMQO | gated | 22.32 | 22.79 | +0.48 |
| LOMQO | learned | 26.56 | 26.86 | +0.30 |

**Why LOMO is barely affected:** on the corrected dataset all six classifier features
(`cost`, `shared_hit`, `shared_read`, `total_buffers`, `io_ratio`, `rows`) are **identical
across all five machines** for a given query — the buffer correction replaced each query's
counts with a machine-invariant value, and `cost`/`rows` never varied by machine. So the
held-out machine's classifier rows are exact duplicates of rows from the other four, and
refitting without them changes almost nothing. The leak was real but, under LOMO,
structurally harmless.

**The consequence that does matter:** six of the thirteen learned-model features
(`dev_cost`, `dev_total_buffers`, `dev_shared_hit`, `dev_shared_read`, `dev_rows`,
`dev_io_ratio`) are therefore **pure functions of `query_id`** — a one-hot encoding of the
query in disguise. Under LOMO every query appears in training, so the GBR can memorise
per-query scaling behaviour rather than learning from workload structure. That is why its
LOQO and LOMQO numbers are the honest measure of what it has actually learned, and why
they should be reported alongside LOMO rather than instead of it.

## 3. Per-held-out-machine breakdown (LOMO, multi-core)

Pooled MAPE hides the single most interesting result in this project, so it is broken out.

| held-out machine | naive-linear | analytical | gated | learned GBR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| c5a | 19.68 | 19.80 | 19.55 | 28.86 |
| c7i | 27.75 | 25.39 | 26.67 | 31.37 |
| m5a | 20.58 | 20.36 | 20.26 | 19.53 |
| r5n | 25.97 | 22.64 | 24.41 | 22.45 |
| z1d | 21.26 | 19.87 | 20.69 | 17.27 |

`c5a` is the hardware outlier (highest bandwidth 14.9, lowest single-core compute). The
learned model degrades sharply there while the formula-based estimators, which need no
training example of a machine to use its measured ratios, degrade gracefully — the
interpolation-not-extrapolation finding.

## 5. Bottleneck classifier

Leave-one-**query**-out, 21 folds. This is the only honest protocol: because the classifier's
features are machine-invariant (see §2), leave-one-machine-out would test on exact duplicates
of training rows.

- **macro-F1 = 0.375**
- trivial always-predict-`mixed` baseline = 0.161

| class | precision | recall | F1 | support |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bandwidth | 0.500 | 0.750 | 0.600 | 20 |
| compute | 1.000 | 0.333 | 0.500 | 15 |
| io | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 20 |
| mixed | 0.400 | 0.400 | 0.400 | 50 |

Confusion matrix (rows = true, columns = predicted):

|  | bandwidth | compute | io | mixed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bandwidth | 15 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| compute | 5 | 5 | 0 | 5 |
| io | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 |
| mixed | 10 | 0 | 20 | 20 |

**The 0.562 figure that appears in older documents is wrong.** It was computed on the
buffer-bug dataset. On the corrected dataset the same protocol gives
0.375, and `io` recall is 0.000.

These labels are 21 hand-assigned judgement calls, not measurements (Q2 and Q13 are
acknowledged coin flips), and because the features are machine-invariant the classifier is
effectively a 21-row lookup table. Replacing the labels with measured resource elasticity
is Tier 1 of `TASKS.md`.

## 6. Measurement noise

The collection protocol specified rejecting any instance with timing CV > 5%, but the metric
was never carried into the dataset. It is now a stored column
(`results/canonical_measurement_cv.csv`).

| statistic | all 20 repetitions | warm 19 (used) |
|---|---:|---:|
| median CV | 2.48% | 0.54% |
| mean CV | 9.68% | 1.55% |
| max CV | 119.98% | 16.50% |
| cells over the 5% threshold | 42 / 105 | 11 / 105 |

105 cells (machine × query), 20 repetitions each, **1 discarded as warmup** → 19 used.

Noisiest remaining cells: r5n/q6 (16.5%), z1d/q19 (9.2%), c7i/q19 (9.1%), c7i/q5 (7.3%), c7i/q8 (6.8%).

### The cold-cache first repetition — a data-quality defect found by this audit

Carrying the CV metric into the dataset for the first time immediately exposed a problem
the project had never recorded: **repetition 1 of each cell is a cold-cache run.**

| observation | value |
|---|---:|
| cells where repetition 1 is the slowest of 20 | 61 / 105 |
| median repetition-1 slowdown vs the warm median | 1.02x |
| worst repetition-1 slowdown | 8.33x |

Example — `z1d`/`q3`: 7612.3 ms, then nineteen runs between 911.8 and 916.3 ms. The cell's
CV is 120.0% including that run and 0.1% without it.

What it contaminates, per cell, if the warmup run is kept:

| target | cells inflated > 5% | worst inflation |
|---|---:|---:|
| p50 | 0 / 105 | 1.007x |
| p95 | 17 / 105 | 1.368x |
| p99 | 46 / 105 | 6.922x |

**The p50 headline is unaffected** — with one outlier among twenty runs the median barely
moves (worst case 0.7%), so every `scaling_factor_p50` result in this file stands whichever
policy is used.

**Every p95 and p99 result published before this audit is contaminated.** At n=20 the 95th
and 99th percentiles sit at the very top of the sorted sample — exactly where the cold-cache
run lands. So those targets were substantially measuring first-run page-cache misses rather
than warm tail latency. This is the most likely explanation for the previously reported
quantile under-coverage (80.7% empirical at nominal 95%, 94.4% at nominal 99%): the models
were being asked to predict a statistic that was itself an artifact. Any p95/p99 number,
calibration table, or p99-based SLA-gate result from before this change must be regenerated.

## 7. Known inconsistency, not yet fixed

`models/hardware_signature.pkl` and `gate/cetp.yml` still carry the **old single-core**
compute scores (c5a 0.593, c7i 0.807, …). The headline result requires the **multi-core**
aggregate scores (c5a 40.81, c7i 25.89, …). **The deployed gate therefore does not embody
the headline finding.** Fixing it means regenerating the shipped models and re-running the
gate's 24 tests; tracked in `TASKS.md`.

## 8. What these numbers do and do not support

Supported: on 5 EBS-backed EC2 instance types at SF1, with 21 TPC-H queries, a roofline
formula weighted by bottleneck probabilities and driven by a **multi-core** compute signal
beats a pure bandwidth-ratio baseline by a small but bootstrap-significant margin, and
formula-based estimators extrapolate to unseen hardware better than the learned model.

Not supported: any claim about hardware outside these 5 instance types, about non-EBS
storage, about scale factors other than SF1, about concurrent workloads, about queries
outside these 21, or about how *often* a new machine behaves like the c5a outlier (n=1).
The `io` bottleneck class reflects buffer-touch patterns under a single uniform storage
backend, not storage diversity.
